subject: Invoice stacking causing seller-credit attribution mismatch
messages:
From: EdgeScale Billing <billing@edgescale.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: payments@edgescale.com
Date: Fri, 03 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice STK-4432: stacked lines applied to wrong seller entity

Hi Marissa,

We need your help reconciling Invoice STK-4432 (attached). During our mid-month payout run we discovered a set of stacked invoice lines that caused an automated seller credit to be issued to the wrong legal entity. The affected usages reference marketplace-usage-ids: MU-8891 / MU-8892 and seller IDs S-ACME-EU and S-ACME-UK. Our system aggregated the credit to S-ACME-UK when the order-of-record indicates S-ACME-EU should receive the credit.

Impact: seller credit of €28,430 issued to wrong entity; payout withhold flagged for VAT holdback. ACME Finance flagged this as an EU VAT exposure and asked for corrected invoice evidence before release.

Attachments: Invoice_STK-4432.pdf (invoice with line items).

Questions:
- Can Redwood confirm which marketplace entity mapping you have for MU-8891/MU-8892?
- Do you require our ledger extract (we can provide CSV) showing the payout routing for the affected batch?
- Any preferred remediation (refund + credit re-issue vs manual ledger adjustment)?

We can provision a ledger extract and evidence bundle by EOD if that helps.

Thanks,
Dana Winters
EdgeScale Billing Operations
EdgeScale Marketplace
billing@edgescale.com

I’m looping in Karhtik (tax) and Marcus (payments ledger) to confirm what evidence we need for EU VAT release. If this is a simple attribution error we prefer a reissued credit to the correct entity; if DocuSign/approval is needed we will coordinate.

Following up with tax context. I reviewed the partial ledger snippet Marissa pasted into the drive folder (thanks, Dana, for uploading). High level: the economic activity for MU-8891/8892 originates in the EU region and should be attributed to S-ACME-EU for VAT purposes. The incorrect aggregation to S-ACME-UK is likely a mapping priority bug where the marketplace router favored a canonical seller id tied to legacy UK registration.

Recommendation:
1) Reissue the seller credit to S-ACME-EU and provide a corrected invoice (credit invoice referencing original STK-4432).
2) Provide ACME with a tax-evidence bundle: (a) original invoice, (b) corrected credit invoice, (c) ledger extract with corrected routing, and (d) seller VAT registration extract.
3) If a holdback was applied, include a short cover letter that explains the remediation and confirms no additional VAT due because the reallocated credit reverses the earlier misattribution.

Marcus: once EdgeScale confirms the reissue approach, we need a timestamped ledger patch that shows the reversal + re-credit. Marcus — can you draft the ledger adjustment template (CSV) we prefer to receive from vendors? I’ve attached our internal mapping file for reference.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Tax & Compliance — Redwood Inference
